subject: CHEMISTRY

core1_titles.CAP-READ-FORMULA: Read a chemical formula before calculating
core1_titles.CAP-ATTACH-SPECIES-ROLE: Attach a role only after tracking the species

QF-FORMULA-PARSING.H1_NOTICE: Notice where the numeral is written: upper right or lower right?
QF-FORMULA-PARSING.H2_RULE_MODEL_REPRESENTATION: A superscript at the upper right gives the overall ionic charge; a subscript counts atoms within the formula.
QF-FORMULA-PARSING.H3_START: Circle the superscript 2− and label it ‘species charge’ before evaluating the options.

QF-PARTICLE-SYMBOLIC-TRANSLATION.H1_NOTICE: Count the separate H₂O particles in the diagram before choosing a symbolic form.
QF-PARTICLE-SYMBOLIC-TRANSLATION.H2_RULE_MODEL_REPRESENTATION: A leading coefficient counts whole particles or formula units; changing a subscript changes the composition of one particle.
QF-PARTICLE-SYMBOLIC-TRANSLATION.H3_START: Write H₂O once for each drawn particle, then combine identical particles with one leading coefficient.

QF-CONSERVATION-CHECK.H1_NOTICE: Count H and O atoms separately on both sides of the equation.
QF-CONSERVATION-CHECK.H2_RULE_MODEL_REPRESENTATION: A coefficient multiplies every atom in the formula that follows it.
QF-CONSERVATION-CHECK.H3_START: Make a two-row ledger for H and O and calculate the left-side and right-side counts before reading the options.

QF-CONDITION-PRESERVATION.H1_NOTICE: Inspect the annotation attached to the reaction arrow; it is part of the source meaning.
QF-CONDITION-PRESERVATION.H2_RULE_MODEL_REPRESENTATION: A condition written over or with a reaction arrow is neither a reactant nor a product and must stay attached to the reaction description.
QF-CONDITION-PRESERVATION.H3_START: Copy the reaction meaning while explicitly retaining the word ‘heat’ as the recorded condition.

QF-SPECIES-ROLE.H1_NOTICE: Use the shown half-change and look at which side contains electrons.
QF-SPECIES-ROLE.H2_RULE_MODEL_REPRESENTATION: A reactant that loses electrons is oxidised and acts as the reducing agent because it supplies electrons to the other species.
QF-SPECIES-ROLE.H3_START: From Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻, mark Zn as the electron-losing reactant before assigning the agent name.

QF-FORMULA-PARSING: Read the ion exactly as written and separate the subscript from the superscript.
Identify ₄ as the oxygen-count subscript and ²⁻ as the overall ionic charge.
Compare that meaning with every option before selecting the answer.
QF-PARTICLE-SYMBOLIC-TRANSLATION: Identify each drawn particle as H₂O without changing its internal composition.
Represent the count with a leading coefficient, giving 2H₂O rather than changing subscripts.
QF-CONSERVATION-CHECK: Apply each coefficient to the complete formula that follows it.
Count 4 H and 2 O atoms on the reactant side.
Count 4 H and 2 O atoms on the product side and compare the ledgers.
QF-CONDITION-PRESERVATION: Read the reaction and the arrow annotation as one source representation.
Identify heat as a recorded reaction condition, not as a reactant, product or coefficient.
Choose the statement that retains the heat condition with the reaction.
QF-SPECIES-ROLE: Track the reactant species through the shown half-change.
Zn appears on the reactant side and produces electrons, so Zn loses electrons and is oxidised.
The electron-losing reactant is the reducing agent; attach the role to Zn only after that change is established.
